citation: Marsh et al. (2020). The Canadian Hydrological Model (CHM) v1.0. Geoscientific Model Development 13, 225-247. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-13-225-2020
description: The Canadian Hydrological Model is an open-source hydrological model built on an unstructured triangular mesh. It supports interchangeable process representations for snow, canopy, frozen-soil infiltration and blowing-snow transport. Inputs include meteorological station or netCDF forcing, mesh geometry, land-surface properties and process settings; outputs include simulated snow and hydrological states as VTK files for spatial inspection. It can run from a single point to a catchment or larger region, with resolution and simulation period selected by the user. Source is free under GPL-3.0 and documentation includes configuration examples. The README warns that its develop branch is always under development and tagged releases are the more stable choices. Much of the documented process suite concerns cold-region surface hydrology, not the full water cycle. It can supply runoff and snowpack information for reservoir or flood studies. Its Bow River SnowCast demonstration is a lead for a separate case study, not proof of current forecast accuracy. A limitation is that its cold-region process set does not yet represent every part of the water cycle.
inputs: Unstructured terrain mesh, land properties and process configuration
